sources.entry: Yape - Yet Another PiP Extension. Finds all HTML5 videos on a webpage and allows you to play them in Picture-in-Picture mode from the Safari toolbar.

summary.one_liner: Yape is a small Safari extension for macOS that finds HTML5 videos on a webpage and plays them in Picture-in-Picture mode from the Safari toolbar.
summary.what_it_does: Yape scans the current webpage for HTML5 video elements and lists them. Clicking an item in the list switches that video to Picture-in-Picture mode. Unlike similar extensions, it adds no buttons to the page itself; PiP is triggered only from the Safari toolbar. The README describes it as very similar to PiPifier and PiedPiPer, which the author found during development. Known issues are listed as open: PiP sometimes requires clicking the page or pressing play first. One previously broken case (coub.com and some gifs on tjournal.ru) is marked as fixed.
use_cases: Watch a webpage video in a floating window while working in other apps
Pop out an HTML5 video from Safari into Picture-in-Picture
Keep a video playing on top while browsing other tabs
Enable PiP without adding overlay buttons to websites
how_to_run: Download the latest Yape.zip from the project releases
Unpack it and copy Yape.app to the Applications folder
In Safari, go to Preferences → Extensions and enable Yape
Open a page with an HTML5 video and pick it from the Yape toolbar list
notable: Triggers PiP from the Safari toolbar rather than adding buttons to web pages
Lists all HTML5 videos found on the current page
Positioned as an alternative to PiPifier and PiedPiPer
caveats: Sometimes needs a click on the page or pressing play before PiP can be enabled
Some sites' videos may not work; the README notes past failures on coub.com and tjournal.ru gifs
